e-3654.problem: Calculate $\dfrac {\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}$ for $y = 3 x^4 + 5x+ \sqrt x.$
e-3654.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{4}+5x+\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{4}+5x+{x}^{1/2}) \\  & =3(4){x}^{3}+5+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =12{x}^{3}+5+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12{x}^{3}+5+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}) \\  & =12(3){x}^{2}+0+\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2}){x}^{-3/2} \\  & =36{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{-3/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-3655.problem: Given $y = \dfrac {3 x^2 + x - 1} x$, find $\dfrac {\textrm d^{3} y} {\textrm d x^3}.$
e-3655.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can rewrite the function as the sum of powers of $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{3{x}^{2}+x-1}{x} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}}{x}+\frac{x}{x}-\frac{1}{x} \\  & =3x+1-{x}^{-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x+1-{x}^{-1}) \\  & =3+0-(-1){x}^{-2} \\  & =3+{x}^{-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3+{x}^{-2}) \\  & =0+(-2){x}^{-3} \\  & =-2{x}^{-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, computing the third derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{x}^{-3}) \\  & =-2(-3){x}^{-4} \\  & =6{x}^{-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate d2ydx2 for y=5x4+4x2.

a
60x2+12
b
60x2+8
c
60x3+8
d
30x2+8
e
60x2+8x
Submit

decision.explanation: Applying the power rule gives dy/dx=20x^3+8x. Differentiating again gives d²y/dx²=60x^2+8, matching option b.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{4}+4{x}^{2}) \\  & =4\cdot 5{x}^{3}+2\cdot 4x \\  & =20{x}^{3}+8x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(20{x}^{3}+8x) \\  & =3\cdot 20{x}^{2}+8 \\  & =60{x}^{2}+8.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Write y=ln(x)+(1/6)x^{-2}. Then y'=1/x-(1/3)x^{-3}, and y''=-1/x^2+x^{-4}=1/x^4-1/x^2, matching option e.

after.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x+\frac{1}{6{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x+\frac{1}{6}{x}^{-2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{6}\cdot (-2){x}^{-2-1} \\  & ={x}^{-1}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-1}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3}) \\  & =(-1){x}^{-1-1}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-3){x}^{-3-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
